title: Your ticket is not a hostage contract
learning_goal: Recognize a sunk-cost mistake and compare future consequences instead of trying to recover irrecoverable spending
subject: psychology
must_not_claim: All past costs are irrelevant when they affect future obligations or recoverable value
Ignoring sunk costs means always quitting
The movie ticket can be refunded
This hypothetical example is an observed experiment

approved_facts.statement: In this hypothetical example, Peter paid $20 for a nonrefundable movie ticket. He dislikes the movie and has one hour remaining. The $20 cannot be recovered by either staying or leaving.
A sunk cost is an already incurred cost that cannot be recovered. The sunk-cost effect is allowing such past expenditure to motivate continuing an endeavor.

For this simplified movie decision, compare the expected enjoyment and other future costs of spending the next hour watching versus leaving. The nonrefundable $20 is the same under both choices and does not favor either option.

Ignoring sunk costs does not mean always quitting. Staying is reasonable if the remaining movie is expected to be worthwhile compared with the alternative; otherwise leaving can avoid wasting more time.
